excerpts: Dreadful SHIPWRECK!! The following account of the shipwreck of the Two Sisters of Rhode-Island, is taken from a Hand-Bill published at BANTRY-BAY, AUG. 12, '97. This morning about 2 o'clock, as some of our fishing boats were working out between the heads, they saw a large ship in the Offing, seemingly in great distress. They stood for the ship, and about 10 o'clock, they boarded her; but there was only one living man on board. She proves to be the Two Sisters, from Rhode-Island, bound for Bristol, and had been out five weeks:—Such a wreck, surely never was seen before! her mizen-mast was all split to pieces, and her main-mast was a stern hanging by some of the wreck; her foremast was also split to pieces, and her fore-top-mast gone by the cap in her steerage or half deck. There were seven men burnt to a coal, and the mate lying under the windlass dead; and as for the Captain, we have no account of him, only the young man found with the wreck says that the Captain and all hands were on deck when some dreadful thunder and lightning came on; and that there were six men on the main-top-sail yard when the mainmast went over the side, and that they were all lost. He says the Captain was on the quarter deck when the mast went, but as he did not see him afterwards, he thinks the wreck hauled him overboard.

excerpts: PHILADELPHIA, Jan. 28. Melancholy Event. Never since we have assumed the office of recording passing events to the public, have we entered on the task with more painful sensations, than on the melancholy occasion we have now to mention. About 5 o'clock yesterday morning the house of Mr. ANDREW BROWN, Printer of the Philadelphia Gazette, in this city, was discovered to be on fire. How it originated or progressed, we have not correct information, but the melancholy and almost unparalleled catastrophe, is, we fear, too certain. Mrs. BROWN, two daughters, one son, and a negro boy, have perished in the flames. Two apprentices have suffered severely, and Mr. BROWN is so dreadfully burnt, that but faint hopes of his recovery are entertained.
